title: No por... deja de: matizar sin negar del todo

sections.content: No por + [reason] + deja de + infinitive ("just because X, it doesn't stop being Y") concedes a limiting fact without letting it cancel out a larger truth -- the perfect closing move for weighing Cuba's small size and its guerrillas' frequent failures against its outsized regional impact. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: No por haber triunfado en un país relativamente pequeño deja de haber sido la Revolución cubana un fenómeno de alcance verdaderamente continental.
items.english: Just because it triumphed in a relatively small country doesn't mean the Cuban Revolution wasn't a phenomenon of truly continental reach.

items.spanish: No por haber fracasado la mayoría de estos intentos guerrilleros deja de haber transformado profundamente el mapa político de la región.
items.english: Just because most of these guerrilla attempts failed doesn't mean they didn't profoundly transform the region's political map.

items.spanish: Cuba demostró que un cambio revolucionario genuino era, después de todo, posible.
items.english: Cuba showed that genuine revolutionary change was, after all, possible.

items.spanish: Prácticamente ningún gobierno latinoamericano pudo ignorar la sombra de la revolución que había triunfado en la isla en 1959.
items.english: Practically no Latin American government could ignore the shadow of the revolution that had triumphed on the island in 1959.

sections.content: The subject of both halves in no por... deja de must be the same -- here, "the Cuban Revolution" (haber triunfado... haber sido) -- since it's one thing whose small scale doesn't cancel out its large impact, not two different things being compared.
